theater: 安達魯西亞海岸與塞維利亞

battle.name: 維京人突襲西班牙
battle.theater: 安達魯西亞海岸與塞維利亞
battle.brief: 八三九年夏，一支自羅亞爾河口南下的北歐船隊洗劫安達魯西亞，溯瓜達基維爾河直抵塞維利亞，擄走科爾多瓦總督易卜拉欣·雅庫布與教會財貨，隨即北返。卡面的羅馬重步兵並非戰場實物：九世紀的西班牙早已沒有軍團，它的用處是點出這場衝突的樞紐——重裝步兵靠兵源與補給線，而雙方缺的正是那條線。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 839年的交戰方只有兩邊，但兩邊都不是國家。北方是「瓦蘭吉亞人」——來自丹麥與斯堪的納維亞的船主、戰士與王的私掠聯合體，沒有常備國防軍，靠分贖金、戰利品與航線維持，統率權分散在各個首領與小王手中，兵力隨季節與戰利品多寡膨脹。南方是科爾多瓦的伍麥葉（倭馬亞）王朝，即阿拔斯王朝在安達魯西亞的政權：埃米爾阿卜杜勒拉赫曼二世是最高統帥，塞維利亞由總督（瓦利）坐鎮，防守靠王室的禁衛、當地的安達魯西亞重騎，以及按部落徵召、按年輪替的「軍德」部隊；各部族之間的效忠靠土地分封與歲貢維持，軍隊因此一來一散，徵召速度取決於首領的意願。安達魯西亞並非單獨面對北方人：同一批船隊在幾個月前剛洗劫過法國的羅亞爾河下游，而法蘭克王國的編年史在同一年記錄北歐人進襲薩克森與圖林根、弗里西人起義；不久之後，維京人還會沿同樣的海岸進入伊比利亞半島南端。換句話說，839年不是孤立事件，而是北歐人南進這條長線上的一個節點，它剛好落在伊比利亞最富庶的一段海岸上。
countriesEn: The two sides in the raid of 839 were not two states. To the north were the Wāringjar, the privateers, shipowners, warriors and kings of Denmark and Scandinavia: a confederation with no standing national army, sustained by shares of ransom money, plunder and control of shipping lanes, with command scattered among individual leaders and petty kings, and a strength that swelled or shrank with the season and the size of the haul. To the south was the Umayyad (Abbasid) emirate of Córdoba, the Abbasid polity in al-Andalus: the emir Abd al-Rahman II was the supreme commander, Seville was held by a wālī, and the defence rested on the caliphal guard, on Andalusi heavy cavalry, and on tribal contingents (jund) levied, paid and rotated year by year; loyalty between the tribes was held together by grants of land and annual tribute, so the army assembled and dispersed again according to the willingness of its chiefs, and the speed of mustering depended on whether those chiefs chose to come. al-Andalus was not facing the northmen alone: the same fleet had stripped the lower Loire only months earlier, and the Frankish annals for that same year record Northmen attacks in Saxony and Thuringia together with a Frisian revolt; a little later the same Vikings would sail into the southern tip of the Iberian Peninsula. In other words, 839 was not an isolated event but one node on the long line of Norse expansion, and it happened to fall on the wealthiest stretch of coastline in Iberia.
people: 安達魯西亞方面的主角是埃米爾阿卜杜勒拉赫曼二世（在位822至852年），他坐鎮科爾多瓦，這場掠奪正好發生在他整合王權、把軍隊與稅收握在手中的關鍵期。真正被捲入戰場的是科爾多瓦總督易卜拉欣·雅庫布，此人在八三〇年代初的宮廷政變裡是手握兵權的一方，八三九年隨軍駐在塞維利亞城內時被北歐人擄走，隨後被帶往北方，一度淪為人質。安達魯西亞方面的另一位要角是阿爾加爾維的總督，他與塞維利亞的守軍同樣吃了敗仗；編年史對他的記載殘缺，只留下他被殺或被擄的結果。真正留下文字的是十世紀的安達魯西亞史家伊本·伊德拉尼——他記下的這一段，是我們知道一八三九年發生了什麼的主要來源。北方那邊反而沒有留下名字：瓦蘭吉亞人的首領與他們的「王」在阿拉伯編年史裡只是整體，沒有留下個人名；北方的記憶反而留在器物與傳說裡，例如後世把這次遠征與丹麥或瑞典王權的崛起連在一起，但這類連繫多屬推測。可以確定的只有三件事：出手的是一支有組織的船隊；它在北方必須有一個能談贖金的政治對手；它帶回足夠的財富與俘虜，讓北方願意接納這批回來的人。
peopleEn: The central figure on the Andalusi side was the emir Abd al-Rahman II (r. 822–852), who ruled from Córdoba at exactly the moment when he was consolidating royal authority and bringing the army and the tax revenue under his own hand. The man actually drawn into the fighting was the wālī of Córdoba, Ibrahim ibn Yaqub, who had held real military authority during the court coups of the early 830s and who was captured inside Seville in 839 while the city was being overrun; he was then carried north and held as a hostage. The other named figure is the wālī of the Algarve district, who shared the defeat of Seville's defenders; the chronicle is fragmentary about him and leaves only his death or his capture. The man who left the writing is Ibn Idrani, a tenth-century Andalusi historian whose chronicle preserves the fullest account of what happened in 839. The north left no names at all: in the Arabic chronicle the Wāringjar leaders and their king appear only as a body, and the northern memory survives instead in objects and in legend — later writers link the expedition to the rise of Danish or Swedish kingship, but such links are speculation. Three things can be asserted: the attack was made by an organised fleet; it required a political counterpart in the north capable of negotiating a ransom; and it brought back enough wealth and captives for the north to be willing to absorb the returning men.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬重步兵在八三九年的西班牙並不是制式裝備，而是對照件：西羅馬在伊比利亞的統治在八世紀初便隨拜占庭人的撤出而告終，軍團、分段鎏甲、大弧面重盾與重標槍早已退出這片土地。真正在塞維利亞城下的，是北方與南方各自的九世紀裝備。北方人帶來的是船：狹長的北歐戰船，淺吃水、可在河口與潟湖上行、能從沙洲間穿過，艏有撞角，長槳在靠岸時可轉作臨時掩體，船上運載斧、矛、標槍與圓盾；真正穿得起鎖子甲的是王的近衛與有產的船主，多數人靠木盾與皮甲，甲胄在北方的流動戰裡要靠船運，靠岸之後大多數人就成了脫了甲的散兵。南方這邊，塞維利亞守軍的裝備來自更東方的傳統：源自東方的阿拔斯與拜占庭系統鎖子甲經地中海商路進口，配尖頂附鼻護的頭盔；步兵是軍德中的標槍兵與斧盾手，弓手用複合弓，騎兵用直身彎刀與標槍，核心是安達魯西亞重騎與柏柏爾輕騎的搭配。攻城一方能依靠的只有城牆：塞維利亞城牆沿用羅馬殖民城希斯帕利斯的舊線，羅馬式的城門與塔樓在九世紀仍在使用——北歐人破城，走的正是這座羅馬城市的門洞。卡面與戰場的真正交集就在這裡：重步兵的制度記憶在這條海岸上並沒有消失，它只是從軍團變成了城牆，從裝備變成了地勢。
kitsEn: The Roman legionary on the card was not field equipment in Spain in 839; it is a reference piece. By the end of the seventh and the opening of the eighth century the Roman administration of Iberia had already gone with the withdrawal of the Byzantines, and the legion, the segmented cuirass, the deep convex scutum and the heavy pilum had long since left the peninsula. What actually stood under the walls of Seville in 839 was the ninth-century equipment of two different systems. The northmen brought ships: narrow northern war-ships of shallow draft, able to work up estuaries and through lagoons and to cross shoals, with a beaked prow, oars that could be turned into a breastwork once the ships were beached, and axe, spear, javelin and round shield carried in the hulls; the men who could afford mail were the king's immediate retainers and the shipowners with property, and for everyone else a wooden shield and leather armour had to do — armour that in mobile northern warfare had to travel by ship, and once the ships were beached, most of the men fought stripped of it. On the Andalusi side the equipment of Seville's garrison came from a tradition further east: mail of the Abbasid and Byzantine systems, imported through Mediterranean trade, worn with conical helmets carrying nasal guards; the infantry of the jund were javelin men and axe-and-shield men, the archers used composite bows, the cavalry fought with straight swords and javelins, and the core of the force was the pairing of Andalusi heavy horse with Berber light horse. The besiegers had only the city wall to work with: Seville's defences ran along the line of the Roman colonia of Hispalis, and Roman gates and towers were still in use in the ninth century — the northmen walked into the city through a Roman gateway. That is where the card and the battlefield genuinely meet: the institutional memory of heavy infantry had not vanished from this coast, it had changed from a legion into a wall, and from equipment into terrain.
tactics: 北方人的戰術核心是海路機動與突然性，而不是正面會戰。船隊在法國西岸與比斯開灣一帶游移一段時間，取得補給與情報後，趁夏末航線與天氣配合南下，避開安達魯西亞海軍的主要基地，在防守薄弱或守軍分散的海岸段落登陸；登岸後不與當地重騎在開闊地硬碰，而是以船為浮動堡壘，控制河口與海路，切斷城與內陸的聯繫，逼守軍在不利時機出城作戰，隨時可以退回船上再出海。北方人一旦得手就帶走人質與財貨迅速北撤，這是一套「打完就跑」的戰法：目標不是佔領土地，而是把可以變成贖金和戰利品的東西搬走；登岸後的短兵相接則以圓盾結盾牆、用短兵器與斧頭近身砍殺，核心是王的近衛那批穿鎖子甲的人。守方這邊，塞維利亞依托羅馬城牆、港口與瓜達基維爾河布防，禁衛與軍德部隊在城郊集結，軍德騎兵以安達魯西亞式的騎射與包抄消耗登陸者，一有機會就以重騎衝擊。關於安達魯西亞海軍有一個流傳很廣的說法：出海攔截的艦隊在暴風中全數覆沒；此說在學界多被視為附會，但足以說明當時雙方都把海軍視為這場衝突的關鍵，因為誰控制海，誰就控制誰能把船開進河裡。
tacticsEn: The northern tactic was built on movement by sea and surprise, not on a set-piece battle. The fleet moved along the French coast and in the Bay of Biscay for a time, taking in supplies and information, and then, with the season and the weather cooperating, ran south; it avoided the main bases of the Andalusi navy, picked a stretch of coast where the defence was thin or the garrisons scattered, and landed there. Once ashore it did not stand and fight the Andalusi heavy horse in the open: it used the ships as floating strongholds, held the river mouth and the sea route, cut the city's links with the interior, and forced the defenders to leave the walls at a moment of their choosing, while the option of getting back aboard and sailing away again was always open. The northmen took what could be turned into ransom and plunder and then withdrew north quickly: the object was never to occupy territory but to carry off the things that could be converted into money, and the close fighting ashore came down to a wall of round shields, hand axes and short blades, with the mail-clad men of the king's household as the hard core. On the defensive side Seville relied on the Roman wall, the harbour and the Guadalquivir, with the guard and the jund units assembling outside the city, and the jund cavalry using Andalusi mounted archery and envelopment to grind down the men who had come ashore, counterattacking with the heavy horse whenever the chance came. On the Andalusi navy there is a very widely repeated story: the squadron that sailed out to intercept the raiders was destroyed by a storm. Most scholars treat that as embellishment, but it is a useful indication of how both sides judged the navy to be the crux of the affair, because whoever controls the sea controls who may sail up the river.
data: 可查證的數字不多，得多數要靠估算。一八三九年與伊歷二二五年交界，阿拉伯編年史把事件記在伊歷二二五年，西歐史家一般把它定在一八三九年夏末，月份只能取個大概。行程是這一役最硬的數字：船隊從法國的羅亞爾河口南下，繞過比斯開灣、沿伊比利亞大西洋岸到直布羅陀海峽，再東行進入地中海直抵瓜達基維爾河口，沿海路約一千五百到一千七百公里；從科爾多瓦到塞維利亞的內河航程約一百二十公里。贖金有明確記載：埃米爾為換回被擄的科爾多瓦總督，付出三千第納爾，並取回被掠走的教會器物。船數沒有留下數字，阿拉伯編年史只說是一支大船隊，而六十餘艘一類的數字屬於十七年之後另一支更大的艦隊，兩者不能混用。城市規模只能作量級判斷：塞維利亞是科爾多瓦政權的第二大城，九世紀的學界估算在數萬人上下，誤差以數千計；科爾多瓦才是這個哈里發國的首府，至十世紀初的估算已達數萬甚至十萬量級。城防可量的是羅馬希斯帕利斯城牆的周長，約五公里量級，雙層城門的通道只容小車與隊伍通行，這意味著登岸的北歐人若要進入城門，必須排成單列。
dataEn: Few verifiable figures survive and most of them are estimates. The year 839 sits at the boundary between the Christian and the Islamic calendars: the Arabic chronicle assigns the event to AH 225, while Western historians generally place it in the late summer of 839, so the month can only be given approximately. The one hard number is the distance covered: the fleet ran from the mouth of the Loire in France, around the Bay of Biscay, along the Atlantic coast of Iberia to the Strait of Gibraltar, and then east into the Mediterranean as far as the mouth of the Guadalquivir — some fifteen hundred to seventeen hundred kilometres of coastal sailing; the inland river run from Córdoba to Seville is about a hundred and twenty kilometres. The ransom is explicitly recorded: the emir paid three thousand dinars to recover the captured wālī of Córdoba and to get back the church plate that had been carried off. No figure survives for the number of ships: the Arabic chronicle speaks only of a great fleet, and numbers in the region of sixty or more belong to the far larger expedition of two decades later and must not be merged with this one. The size of the towns can only be judged by order of magnitude: Seville was the second city of the Córdoba polity, and scholarly estimates for the ninth century put it in the tens of thousands, with an error of several thousand either way; Córdoba was the capital, and estimates for the early tenth century already reach the tens or even hundreds of thousands. What can be measured about the defences is the Roman wall of Hispalis, whose circuit was on the order of five kilometres and whose double gateway admitted only wagons and files of men in single column — which means that the northmen who came ashore could only enter the city in a narrow line.
cause: 維京人南下不是偶然的機緣，而是一條被結構性因素推動的路線。丹麥與斯堪的納維亞面臨的人口、耕地與冬季生計壓力，使一批武裝船主在八三〇年代離開家鄉，在北海、波羅的海與英格蘭一帶尋找戰利品；法蘭克王國內戰與加洛林王朝的分裂，提供了大量可乘之機，而羅亞爾河口那樣的咽喉地點，成為襲擾不列顛與法國西部的基地。但要從北海闖進伊比利亞，還需要另一種誘因：安達魯西亞的財富。科爾多瓦的哈里發國靠稅收、農業與遠程貿易積累金銀，塞維利亞又是瓜達基維爾河的出口與徵稅節點，港口裡有來自歐洲、非洲與亞洲的貨物，而科爾多瓦的統治者同時是基督徒，教堂的銀器與金屬祭器在北方的戰利品市場上有價。於是一次為錢而來的劫掠，恰好鎖定了一個有錢、有港、有城牆、又有可回報之物的目標。安達魯西亞這邊也有自己的算盤：總督易卜拉欣·雅庫布在宮廷派系鬥爭中的位置並不穩，埃米爾需要把他放在塞維利亞這樣的關口上；北歐人擄走他，等於在科爾多瓦的政治棋盤上直接掀了一枚棋子。雙方之間並沒有預謀：對北方人而言，目標是財貨；對南方而言，防禦真正的破口不是城牆，而是海岸線與河口從未被當成前線來守。
causeEn: The Viking move south was not a chance accident but a route pushed along by structural pressures. Population, farmland and the winter economy of Denmark and Scandinavia pushed a body of armed shipowners out of their homeland in the 830s, hunting plunder in the North Sea, the Baltic and England; the civil wars inside the Frankish kingdom and the fragmentation of the Carolingian dynasty offered opportunity on a large scale, and a place like the mouth of the Loire became a base for raiding Britain and western France. But breaking into Iberia from the North Sea required a different kind of inducement: the wealth of al-Andalus. The Córdoba caliphate accumulated gold and silver through taxation, agriculture and long-distance trade, Seville was the export and customs point at the mouth of the Guadalquivir, its harbour held goods from Europe, Africa and Asia, and the rulers of Córdoba were Christians, so the church plate and metal altar vessels of Seville had a price in the northern market for plunder. A raid made for money therefore locked onto a target that was rich, had a harbour, had walls, and had something worth carrying away. The Andalusi side had its own calculation as well: the wālī Ibrahim ibn Yaqub was not secure in the factional struggles at court, and the emir needed such a man posted at a gateway such as Seville; the northmen's capture of him amounted to overturning a piece on the political board in Córdoba. None of this was arranged between the two sides: for the northmen the object was wealth, and for the south the real gap in the defence was not the wall but the coastline and the river mouths, which were never treated as a front.
impact: 這場劫掠的直接後果分兩頭。在安達魯西亞一頭，塞維利亞的教產與市面遭劫，埃米爾為贖回總督付出的三千第納爾，以及他讓外敵把人從自己城裡帶走這件事，同樣被記在後世編年史裡，成為他執政生涯的一段罵名；安達魯西亞海軍的問題、海岸線缺乏海防部署的問題，也正是在這一連串事件之後才被認真處理的。塞維利亞隨後加強了港口與城門的守備，瓜達基維爾河上的攔截與水警機制逐步建立，北方人的下一次來襲因此比這一次更難得手。在北方一頭，金銀、教會器物與俘虜大量流入斯堪的納維亞，成為丹麥王權積累財富的重要來源之一：八四〇年代末，挪威的哈拉爾·克拉克能拿出巨款向法蘭克教廷輸誠，很大程度上靠的就是這十年間的掠奪收入。編年史記載北方人把俘虜帶回去、與北方的王一起生活，最後以贖金換回，這說明維京式的掠奪並不是孤立的暴力，而是有談判、有贖金、有收益核算的生意；也正是這種生意，把北歐人從海盜變成可以遠征的勢力。
impactEn: The immediate consequences of the sack ran in two directions. In al-Andalus, Seville's church property and its markets were hit; the three thousand dinars the emir paid to get the wālī back, and the fact that foreigners were allowed to carry a man out of his own city, were both recorded in later chronicles and became a lasting stain on that reign. The weakness of the Andalusi navy and the absence of any real coastal defence were also taken seriously only after this and the run of events that followed. Seville tightened the watch on its harbour and its gates, the interception system on the Guadalquivir and the water-watch posts were built up step by step, and the next northern raid found the coast harder to take. In the north, gold and silver, church plate and captives flowed into Scandinavia and became one of the main sources of Danish royal wealth: by the late 840s Harald Klak could put up large sums to work his way into favour at the Frankish court, and much of that money came from the plunder of these ten years. The chronicle records that the northmen carried their prisoners home, kept them among the king's people, and finally exchanged them for a ransom, which shows that the Viking raid was not blind violence but a business with negotiation, ransom and accounting; and it was precisely that business that turned pirates into a force capable of long-distance expeditions.
result: 結局是劫掠得手、戰術撤退、贖金成交。塞維利亞的城門被破，總督與阿爾加爾維的總督成為俘虜，教堂器物與兩位聖徒的聖髑被帶往北方；北歐人沒有留下駐軍，沒有宣布佔領，也沒有打算經營這座城市，他們帶著能變成錢的東西沿原路北返，海上追擊沒有成功，安達魯西亞最終以三千第納爾贖回被擄者、取回教產。這一場勝負清楚地顯示：九世紀的安達魯西亞有足以維持帝國的城市與稅收，卻沒有能封住河口的常備艦隊；海上的突然性比城牆的厚度更決定戰局。卡面的羅馬重步兵在此刻顯出它的位置：羅馬人在伊比利亞的軍團制度早已隨帝國西部的崩解而消失，塞維利亞的守軍靠的是軍德徵召與安達魯西亞重騎，北方人靠的是船與王的近衛，兩邊都沒有常備重裝步兵可以倚仗；重裝步兵在九世紀並不是過時，而是被證明在這條戰線上不划算——重裝部隊若沒有穩定的補給線與源源不絕的兵源，就只能在岸上等著被快速掠過的船帶走勝負。
resultEn: The outcome was a successful sack, a tactical withdrawal and a completed ransom. The gates of Seville were broken, the wālī of Córdoba and the wālī of Algarve became prisoners, the plate of the church and the relics of two local saints were carried north; the northmen left no garrison, proclaimed no annexation and had no intention of administering the city, and they took away the things that could be turned into money and went back the way they came, with no successful pursuit at sea, while al-Andalus eventually bought the prisoners back for three thousand dinars and recovered the church property. The balance of the affair was clear: ninth-century al-Andalus had cities and tax revenue sufficient to sustain an empire, but no standing fleet capable of sealing the mouths of its rivers; surprise at sea mattered more to the outcome than the thickness of a wall. The Roman legionary on the card shows its place here: the legionary system of Rome in Iberia had vanished with the collapse of the western empire, Seville's garrison relied on jund levies and Andalusi heavy horse, the northmen relied on their ships and the king's retainers, and neither side had a standing heavy infantry to lean on. Heavy infantry in the ninth century was not so much obsolete as disproved on this front: without a steady supply line and a constant flow of replacements, a heavily armed infantry stays on the shore and waits for a fast ship to carry the verdict away.
